Angular is still a great framework. But after years of working with it, here’s why Vue.js became my preferred choice for many of the projects I build for clients.

6 min read
2 hours ago

--

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Photo by Jackson Sophat on UnsplashI’ve been using Angular for years.
I’ve built projects with it.
I’ve worked with its ecosystem.
I’ve used TypeScript, RxJS, dependency injection, services, routing, forms, and all the other pieces that come with building serious Angular applications.
For a long time, Angular was one of my default choices.
And I still think it’s a very good framework.
But something changed over the years.
For many of my newer client projects, I started choosing Vue.js instead.
Not because Angular suddenly became bad.
Not because Vue.js can magically do everything better.
The reason is much simpler.
For many of the projects I work on, Vue.js lets me get to the result with less friction.
